newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela and China sign Orimulsion deals.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela and China sign Orimulsion deals.

text.p: Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng signed agreements with Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera Wednesday on the supply of trademark boiler fuel Orimulsion to China and a possible joint venture Orimulsion production plant.
The accords were signed at Miraflores presidential palace on the first full day of Li's official visit to Venezuela.

Carlos Borregales, President of Bitumenes de Orinoco (Bitor), a unit of state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), said a first agreement was for the supply of 140,000 tonnes of Orimulsion, as part of on-going tests on the boiler fuel alternative in China.
"We have already conducted very successful tests and now we're going to send a much larger shipment, of 140,000 tonnes, to do tests throughout plants in China," Borregales told reporters.
He said the shipment would leave Venezuela in the first week of December. Bitor started Orimulsion test shipments to China's National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) in August.
The second agreement was on a memorandum of understanding for a feasibility study to build a $320-million plant in Venezuela.
"The plant would have a capacity of five million tonnes ... we hope to conclude the feasibility study by the middle of next year," Borregales said.
That capacity would represent about 25 percent of Venezuela's planned Orimulsion output by the end of the decade. It exported 3.6 million tonnes of the bitumen and water mix fuel in 1995.
The plant would be built in eastern Monagas state, in Cerro Negro area, and China's participation in the joint venture would be 70 percent with the remaining 30 percent from Bitor.
If the project goes ahead, Borregales said the plant will go on stream in the second half of 1999. The whole of its production would go to China.
Asked about planned export revenues, he gave no figures but said Orimulsion was very competitive with coal and "the price of coal in southern China is today about 45 dollars a tonne."
Orimulsion is produced from an extra heavy bitumen-type oil found in large quantities in northern Venezuela.
Venezuela has already supplied contracts for the heavy fuel with power generators in the United States, United Kingdom, Japan, Denmark, Lithuania and Canada.
